definition_zh: 志向；渴望达到的目标；送气发音；吸入；抽吸；一丝气息
definition_en: a strong hope or aim to achieve something, or the act of breathing something in
core_image: 一个人站在海边深吸一口气，眼睛望着对岸还看不见的灯光
scene: 她把想去对岸读书的念头写在信的末尾，写完又对着窗外深吸了一口气。Her aspiration to study abroad survived two failed applications.
sceneCN: 这里 aspiration 指「想要达到的目标与渴望」（第 1 个义项：志向上的愿望）；句意为她想出国读书的志向挺过了两次申请失败。图中可辨识物件：写满字的信纸、窗外对岸的灯光、被吸进胸腔的一口气、两次退回的信封。

pos.zh: 志向；渴望；送气音；吸入；抽吸

derivatives.zh: 基础动词，来自拉丁语「向某处呼气」，语义为「渴望、立志」
由名词加形容词后缀构成，语义由「志向」转为「以志向为标榜的」
由过去分词转为形容词，语义由「送气」转为「带送气的」
由动词词干加表示人的后缀构成，语义由「渴望」转为「追求某职位的人」

senses.title: A hoped-for aim
senses.definition: a strong hope or ambition to achieve something in the future
senses.definitionCN: 对未来取得某物所抱的强烈希望或志向
senses.example: Her aspiration to study abroad survived two failed applications.
senses.exampleCN: 她想出国读书的志向挺过了两次申请失败。
senses.why: the Latin verb meant to breathe toward something, so an aspiration is a breath aimed at a distant object.
senses.whyCN: 那个拉丁动词意为「朝某物呼气」，因此志向就是一缕朝远处目标呼出的气。

senses.title: Longing for high rank
senses.titleCN: 对高位或大成就的渴望
senses.definition: a desire for a high position, honour or a distinguished place
senses.definitionCN: 对高职位、荣誉或显要位置的渴求
senses.example: His aspiration to the chair was known to everyone but him.
senses.exampleCN: 他想坐主席位子的心思，除了他自己，人人都知道。
senses.why: breathing toward a seat of honour is the social form of the same reach.
senses.whyCN: 朝着荣誉之位呼一口气，是同一份伸手在社会层面的形态。

senses.title: Breath released in speech
senses.definition: the audible burst of breath that follows some consonants, as in the p of pin
senses.definitionCN: 某些辅音之后可听见的一股气流，如某些词首那个辅音之后的气
senses.example: The teacher marked the aspiration after the t with a small hook.
senses.exampleCN: 老师在那个辅音之后用一个小钩标出送气。
senses.why: the phonetic sense is the literal one: breath pushed out at the moment of speaking.
senses.whyCN: 语音义是最字面的用法：说话那一刻把气推出来。

senses.title: Drawing foreign matter into the lungs
senses.definition: the entry of food, liquid or other matter into the airway and lungs
senses.definitionCN: 食物、液体或其他物质进入气道与肺部
senses.example: The nurse watched for aspiration during the night feed.
senses.exampleCN: 夜间喂食时护士一直留意有无误吸。
senses.why: here breathing in becomes dangerous because what is drawn in does not belong in the lungs.
senses.whyCN: 这里的「吸」变得危险，因为被吸进去的东西不该在肺里。

senses.title: Removal by suction
senses.definition: the use of suction to draw fluid or tissue out of a cavity
senses.definitionCN: 用负压把液体或组织从腔体中吸出
senses.example: The aspiration of the cyst took less than a minute.
senses.exampleCN: 囊肿的抽吸不到一分钟就完成了。
senses.why: the same drawing motion is turned to medical use, where breath is replaced by a pump.
senses.whyCN: 同一个「吸」的动作被转作医疗用途，只是呼气换成了泵。

senses.title: Drawing fluid up a tube
senses.definition: the lifting of liquid by reduced pressure in an engine, pump or laboratory line
senses.definitionCN: 在发动机、泵或实验管路中借压差把液体吸上来
senses.example: Fuel aspiration failed when the line cracked.
senses.exampleCN: 管路开裂后燃油抽吸失效。
senses.why: machines borrow the word because a pump also pulls matter toward itself by creating a void.
senses.whyCN: 机器借用这个词，因为泵也靠制造空处把物质拉向自己。

senses.title: A breath of air
senses.definition: a single breath or a faint movement of air
senses.definitionCN: 一次呼吸，或空气极轻微的流动
senses.example: An aspiration of wind came through the shutter and moved the ash.
senses.exampleCN: 一丝风从百叶窗里进来，吹动了灰。
senses.why: the oldest physical layer survives in literary use, where the word means the air itself.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的物理层在文学用法里留存，那里这个词指空气本身。

senses.title: Shared hopes of a group
senses.definition: the collective hopes that a community or a generation holds for its future
senses.definitionCN: 一个社群或一代人对自身未来所抱的共同希望
senses.example: The school was built on the aspirations of families who had never had one.
senses.exampleCN: 这所学校建立于那些从未有过学校的家庭的期盼之上。
senses.why: many breaths aimed at one future add up to a public aspiration, which is how politics uses the word.
senses.whyCN: 许多口气朝同一个未来呼出，就汇成一种公共期盼，政治语言正是这样用它的。

intro.en: Aspiration comes from Latin aspiratio 'a breathing upon', from aspirare 'to breathe toward', built on ad- 'to' and spirare 'to breathe'. The deeper origin of spirare is not settled. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: 该词来自拉丁 aspiratio「朝某物呼气」，其动词 aspirare「向……呼气」由 ad-「向」与 spirare「呼吸」构成。spirare 的更深来源尚无定论，年代均为约数。

items.en: Spirare meant 'to breathe, to blow'. Its deeper origin is uncertain; the comparison with a root for 'to blow' is a hypothesis rather than a demonstrated derivation.
items.cn: spirare 意为「呼吸、吹」。其更深来源不确定；把它与表示「吹」的词根相比对，只是假说，并非已证实的派生。

items.en: Ad- 'to' plus spirare gave aspirare 'to breathe upon, to blow toward', and by metaphor to favour or to strive toward.
items.cn: ad-「向」加 spirare 构成 aspirare「朝……呼气、向……吹」，并比喻为「眷顾」或「向往」。

items.en: The noun aspiratio named the breathing and, in grammar, the rough breathing marked over certain letters.
items.cn: 名词 aspiratio 指这股呼气，并在语法中指标在某些字母上的粗气符号。

items.en: English took the noun in the fourteenth century, first for the grammatical sense of rough breathing.
items.cn: 英语在十四世纪吸收了这个名词，最早用于语法上的「粗气」义。

items.en: From the sixteenth century the word was used for a hope directed at a high aim, and the medical suction sense followed in the nineteenth.
items.cn: 从十六世纪起，这个词用于指向高目标的希望；医学上的抽吸义在十九世纪随后出现。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin of spirare and the dating of the hopeful sense): no citation fixes the first use for ambition, and any Indo-European form offered for spirare is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（spirare 的更深来源与希望义的确切年代）：没有书证能定住它首次用于「抱负」的时间；凡为 spirare 给出的印欧语形式均属重构形式。

note.en: Group one separates look-alikes built on the breathing verb from words that only sound similar; group two separates kinds of longing.
note.cn: 第一组区分同出「呼吸」动词的形近词与只是读音相近的词；第二组区分不同类型的渴望。

entries.definition: To aim at something high; the noun is the state, the verb is the reaching.
entries.definitionCN: 朝高处立志；名词是那个状态，动词是那次伸手。

entries.definition: In- 'into' plus spirare: a breathing in, hence the sudden idea that seems to arrive from outside.
entries.definitionCN: 由 in-「入」加 spirare 构成：吸进来，因而指仿佛从外面到来的灵感。

entries.definition: Ex- 'out' plus spirare: breathing out, and by extension the end of a period when time has run out.
entries.definitionCN: 由 ex-「出」加 spirare 构成：呼出，并引申指期限走完的到期。

entries.definition: Re- 'again' plus spirare: the whole cycle of breathing, with no aim attached.
entries.definitionCN: 由 re-「再」加 spirare 构成：整个呼吸循环，不含目标。

entries.definition: From the same sprinkling verb, but it means a casting of doubt or a slander, not a hope.
entries.definitionCN: 同出那个「洒、喷」的动词，但意思是对人泼脏水、造谣中伤，而非希望。

entries.definition: A strong desire to rise in status or power; it is more worldly than aspiration.
entries.definitionCN: 对地位或权力上升的强烈欲望；比 aspiration 更世俗。

entries.definition: A specific end point one works toward; it is the target itself, not the longing for it.
entries.definitionCN: 努力所指向的具体终点；是目标本身，而不是对目标的渴望。

entries.definition: A cherished wish, often distant and not yet planned; it is warmer and looser than aspiration.
entries.definitionCN: 珍爱的愿望，往往遥远且尚无计划；比 aspiration 更温暖也更松散。

entries.definition: A deep and often painful longing; it stresses the ache rather than the plan to achieve.
entries.definitionCN: 深沉而常带痛感的渴望；强调那份渴，而不是实现它的计划。

entries.definition: The amount taken into the body or a machine in a period; it is the plain physical relative of the suction sense.
entries.definitionCN: 一段时间内进入身体或机器的量；是抽吸义最朴素的物理近亲。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The Latin verb means to breathe toward something, so a strong hope is a breath aimed at a far target.
normal.cn: 那个拉丁动词意为「朝某物呼气」，因此一份强烈的希望就是一缕朝远处目标呼出的气。

normal.en: The family runs aspire, aspiration, aspirant, aspirational, aspirated.
normal.cn: 同族词覆盖动词、名词、追求者、愿景式形容词与送气形容词。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the fields: career aspirations, aspiration pneumonia, aspirated consonant.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出领域：职业志向、吸入性肺炎、送气辅音。

normal.en: The same breathing verb gives inspiration, expiration and respiration, each with its own prefix direction.
normal.cn: 同一个「呼吸」动词还给出 inspiration、expiration 与 respiration，各自带有自己的前缀方向。

normal.en: Medical suction keeps the physical picture: something is drawn out of a cavity by reduced pressure.
normal.cn: 医学抽吸保留了物理图景：靠压差把某物从腔体中吸出。

abstract.en: Picture a long breath held while looking across water at lights not yet reachable.
abstract.cn: 想象隔水望着还够不到的灯光时，长长地屏住一口气。

abstract.en: Picture a seed on a sill, leaning toward a window it cannot move to.
abstract.cn: 想象窗台上的一粒种子，朝它无法移动过去的窗子倾斜。

abstract.en: Picture a letter written and rewritten but never sent, kept in a drawer.
abstract.cn: 想象一封写了又改、始终没寄出的信，放在抽屉里。

examples.en: The scholarship matched her aspiration with a place at the college.
examples.cn: 这笔奖学金让她的志向与一个学院名额对上了。

examples.en: Rural families spoke of their aspirations for a clinic of their own.
examples.cn: 乡下家庭谈起他们想要一所自己的诊所的期盼。

examples.en: The doctor ordered suction to prevent aspiration during sleep.
examples.cn: 医生安排了吸痰，以防睡眠中误吸。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「a 斯匹瑞」——朝远处深吸一口气再向前望 → 志向、渴望

root: 拉丁 aspiratio「呼气」← aspirare「向……呼气」= ad-（向）+ spirare（呼吸）；spirare 更深来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one breath: air is aimed at a far object and becomes a hope; the same air is aimed at a seat of honour, then at a consonant, then drawn into a lung, then pulled by a pump, then felt as a faint wind, and finally shared by a whole community.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一口气展开：气朝远处目标呼出而成希望；同一口气再朝荣誉之位、朝一个辅音、进一只肺、被泵抽动、化作一丝风，最后被整个社群共同呼出。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a long breath drawn at the shore while looking at lights across the water.
core.cn: 核心意象：站在岸边望着对岸的灯光，长长吸一口气。

branches.en: THE BREATH AIMED HIGH: hope for an aim and hunger for a seat of honour.
branches.cn: 朝高处呼出的气：对目标的希望，以及对荣誉之位的渴求。

branches.en: THE BREATH HEARD: phonetics keeps the literal push of air.
branches.cn: 被听见的气：语音学保留了最字面的推气。

branches.en: MATTER DRAWN IN: what enters a lung and what a pump pulls up a line.
branches.cn: 被吸进的物质：进入肺里的东西，与泵沿着管路抽上来的东西。

branches.en: MATTER TAKEN OUT: clinical suction reverses the direction and removes.
branches.cn: 被取出的物质：临床抽吸把方向反过来，取走东西。

branches.en: FROM A GUST TO A GENERATION: one faint breath widens into the shared hopes of many.
branches.cn: 从一阵微风到一代人：一丝微弱的气，扩展成许多人的共同期盼。

intro.en: The word is a Latin verb plus a noun suffix, and the same prefix and verb build several common English words, so the family is easy to read by parts.
intro.cn: 这个词是一个拉丁动词加名词后缀，同一个前缀与动词还构成若干常用英语词，因此这一族很容易按部件读出。

latinIntro.en: Latin spirare 'to breathe' gives spirit, inspire, expire, respire and conspire; ad- 'to' appears in adapt, adjacent and admire.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 spirare「呼吸」衍生出 spirit、inspire、expire、respire 与 conspire；ad-「向」见于 adapt、adjacent 与 admire。

items.example: The prefix points the breath at an object.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把气指向某个对象。
这个词根带着呼吸这个动作。

items.example: The wind seemed to strive toward the cliff.
items.exampleCN: 那阵风仿佛朝崖上使劲。

items.example: Her aspiration was to build a clinic.
items.exampleCN: 她的志向是建一所诊所。

items.structure: aspirare passing into French and English
items.example: He aspired to the vacant chair.
items.exampleCN: 他渴望那把空出的椅子。
十名求职者参加了考试。

items.example: The poster was aspirational rather than factual.
items.exampleCN: 这张海报是励志的，而不是写实的。

items.meaning: pronounced with a burst of breath
items.example: The aspirated consonant was hard for the children.
items.exampleCN: 这个送气辅音让孩子们觉得难。

items.meaning: a breathing in, a sudden idea
items.example: The design came in a single inspiration.
items.exampleCN: 这个设计来自一次顿悟。

items.meaning: breathing out, the end of a term
items.example: The lease reached expiration in June.
The spirit of the place was quiet.
items.exampleCN: 这个地方的气息很安静。
